name: Entry Rotunda
read: The double doors grind shut behind you, and the green light of the wood is gone. You stand in a small round chamber of grey stone. Moss grows in the cracks, and the air smells of damp paper and old smoke. A broad orc lies slumped against the wall, grey-skinned and very still, one hand swollen black. Wide archways open to the north and to the south. From somewhere beyond, faint and steady, comes a woman's whispering voice.
notes:
The entrance of the archive. The dead orc is Snag, one of the Bloodtusk band. He opened the strongbox in the Steward's Room (room 4), was pricked by the Rot Needle, and crawled back here to die. His hand is black with the Grey Rot. The whispering is Mother Ysolde, the Leper Oracle, in room 12; it carries through the whole archive and never stops.

No encounter.

Treasure: a Potion of Healing on Snag's belt.

Exits: Mosaic Hall (2, archway), Reading Hall (3, archway). The archway in the middle of the north wall leads into the Mosaic Hall. The archway in the middle of the south wall leads into the Reading Hall. The entrance double doors in the middle of the east wall lead back out to the dark wood.

name: Mosaic Hall
read: A square hall opens before you, its floor laid with a great mosaic of tiny grey and gold tiles. The pattern shows two crowns side by side: one with its points rising like a growing moon, one with its points falling like a fading one. Overturned reading tables have been dragged into a rough wall across the room. Behind them a small fire smoulders, and the hall smells of sweat, smoke and burned meat. Wooden doors stand in the north and east walls.
notes:
The Bloodtusk orcs hold this hall against whatever else lives in the archive. They built the table wall facing south and north, and they have heard the Rot Scribes in room 3 and fear them. The mosaic shows the Waxing Crown and the Waning Crown: a hint that two crown-shaped keys open the stone door in the Hall of the Stone Door (room 8). A DC 12 Intelligence (History) check recognizes them as the twin seals of the Oracle's scribes.

Encounter: 2 Orc Raiders. They fight from behind the tables (half cover). If one falls, the other runs east to warn Gruk Halfear in the Pedestal Hall (room 9).

Treasure: none.

Exits: Entry Rotunda (1, archway), Wizard's Vault (5, door), Steward's Room (4, door). The archway in the middle of the south wall leads back to the Entry Rotunda. The door in the middle of the north wall opens into the Wizard's Vault. The door in the middle of the east wall opens into the Steward's Room.

name: Reading Hall
read: Long writing desks fill this hall in rows, each lit by a squat candle that has burned for longer than any candle should. Grey figures in hooded robes sit hunched at the desks, quills moving across the paper in steady strokes. The scratching of the pens fills the room. The air is thick and sweet, like fruit gone bad, and a fine grey dust lies over everything. An archway opens to the west, and stone stairs lead away to the east.
notes:
The Oracle's scribes died here at their desks, and the Grey Rot raised them. They still copy her prophecies, which they hear as whispering from room 12. They ignore the hero until the hero touches a desk, a page or a scribe, or speaks to them; then all three rise at once. The candles give dim light across the hall.

Encounter: 3 Rot Scribes.

Treasure: a Potion of Healing in a leather satchel hanging from the chair of the scribe nearest the stairs.

Exits: Entry Rotunda (1, archway), Basket Alcove (6, archway), Rubble Chapel (7, stairs). The archway in the middle of the north wall leads back to the Entry Rotunda. The archway in the middle of the west wall leads into the Basket Alcove. The stairs in the middle of the east wall lead to the Rubble Chapel.

name: Steward's Room
read: This narrow room was once an office. A heavy iron strongbox sits on a stone shelf against the wall, its lid closed, a clumsy scratch of orc marks on its front. Torn ledgers lie across the floor, trampled into the dust. The wooden door in the east wall hangs from one hinge, its lock smashed in. Stone stairs climb away to the north, and a cold draught comes down them carrying the smell of old stone.
notes:
The archive's steward kept accounts and stores here. The Bloodtusk orcs smashed the east door and broke through into the Pedestal Hall (room 9), where they now camp. Snag tried the strongbox and the needle killed him slowly (room 1); the orc marks on the box say "death box". The other orcs have left it alone.

Trap: Rot Needle

  • Trigger: a creature tries the strongbox lock without disarming it, by key, pick or force.
  • Find: DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) finds a grey-crusted needle hole in the lock plate, and dried black blood around it.
  • Effect: DC 15 Constitution saving throw [[/save con 15]]; [[/damage 6d10 poison]] on a failure, half on a success. On a failure the creature also has the Poisoned condition for 1 hour.
  • Disarm or avoid: Jam the needle with thieves' tools (DC 15 Dexterity check), or open the box with Mage Hand, or break the hinges from behind with a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check. The needle resets each time the lid is closed.

No encounter.

Treasure: in the strongbox, 50 gp in a cloth bag and a bottle of fine elven wine worth 25 gp, sealed with green wax.

Exits: Hall of the Stone Door (8, stairs), Mosaic Hall (2, door), Pedestal Hall (9, door). The stairs in the middle of the north wall climb to the Hall of the Stone Door. The door in the middle of the west wall opens into the Mosaic Hall. The broken door in the middle of the east wall opens into the Pedestal Hall and the orc camp.

name: Wizard's Vault
read: A small round chamber, its walls lined with empty shelves. In the middle of the floor kneels a man made of violet crystal, every fold of his robe and every hair of his beard turned to glassy stone. One crystal hand reaches toward the floor, and light glints off something small and metal lying just beyond his fingers. A faint hum comes from the stone around him, and the air tastes of metal.
notes:
The kneeling man is Corvin Ashmere, a treasure hunter and wizard who reached the archive before the orcs. He reached for the key and the Crystal Ward turned him to crystal. He is beyond saving by ordinary means (a Greater Restoration does not help; a Wish would). The orcs looked in, saw him, and left.

Trap: Crystal Ward

  • Trigger: a creature comes within 5 feet of Corvin or of the key.
  • Find: DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana) or Wisdom (Perception) notices a ring of faint violet runes in the floor around him, 5 feet out.
  • Effect: DC 15 Constitution saving throw [[/save con 15]]; [[/damage 6d10 force]] on a failure, half on a success. On a failure, violet crystal grows around the creature's legs and it has the Restrained condition; it can end this with an action and a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check, or another creature can break it free the same way.
  • Disarm or avoid: Suppress the ward for 1 minute with a DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana) check, or end it with Dispel Magic; or hook the key out from beyond the ring with a pole, rope or Mage Hand.

No encounter.

Treasure: the Key of the Waxing Crown, on the floor beside Corvin's hand.

Exits: Mosaic Hall (2, door). The door in the middle of the south wall leads back to the Mosaic Hall.

name: Basket Alcove
read: This small round room is quiet and dry. Woven baskets of every size are stacked against the walls, most of them crushed or empty, their contents long since rotted to dust. One medium basket sits apart on a stone ledge, its lid tied down with faded red cord. The smell is of dry reeds and old parchment. The only way out is the archway back to the east.
notes:
The scribes stored finished copies here before they were shelved. The Rot Scribes no longer come here. The basket on the ledge holds the one scroll that survived.

No encounter.

Treasure: a Spell Scroll in the medium basket on the ledge.

Exits: Reading Hall (3, archway). The archway in the middle of the east wall leads back to the Reading Hall.

name: Rubble Chapel
read: At the top of the stairs is a small round chapel. Half of it is filled by a great pile of broken stone: chunks of carved robe, a fist the size of a shield, part of a hooded stone face lying on its side. Dust still hangs in the air. Through a gap in the rubble, low near the floor, a glint of metal catches your light.
notes:
A guardian statue of the Oracle's order stood here. It fell long ago, but its binding remains: when a creature digs into the pile or pulls stones away from the key, the rubble rises as the Rubble Warden. The glint is the second key.

Encounter: 1 Rubble Warden.

Treasure: the Key of the Waning Crown, under the rubble where the Warden stood.

Exits: Reading Hall (3, stairs). The stairs in the middle of the west wall lead back down to the Reading Hall.

name: Hall of the Stone Door
read: At the top of the stairs is a tall, narrow hall. Its eastern wall holds two doors. Near the middle stands a great door of solid grey stone, carved with a crown at its centre and set with two keyholes, each shaped like a small crown. At the far north end of the same wall is a plain stone door, heavy and close-fitting, with no handle on this side. The hall is cold and still, and the whispering sounds closer here.
notes:
The stone door near the middle of the east wall leads to the Inner Archive (room 10). It opens only when both the Key of the Waxing Crown and the Key of the Waning Crown are turned at once; a solo hero can turn one and hold the other in place, or turn them one after the other within a round. It cannot be picked or forced. The plain door at the north end of the east wall leads to the Oracle's Gallery (room 11). It is barred from the far side with a stone bar; from here it opens only with a DC 22 Strength (Athletics) check.

No encounter.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Steward's Room (4, stairs), Inner Archive (10, locked stone door), Oracle's Gallery (11, sealed door). The stairs in the middle of the south wall lead back down to the Steward's Room. The locked stone door with two keyholes in the middle of the east wall opens into the Inner Archive. The sealed stone door at the north end of the east wall opens into the Oracle's Gallery, but only from that side.

name: Pedestal Hall
read: Bookshelves have been tipped over and dragged into a waist-high barricade across this long hall. Behind it are bedrolls, gnawed bones and a cookfire that fills the room with smoke and red light. At the far end a stone pedestal holds a small glass flask, and the liquid inside seems to bend the light around it. Crude red tusks are daubed on the shelves. Doors stand in the west wall and the north wall.
notes:
The camp of the Bloodtusk orcs. They broke in through the west door from the Steward's Room (room 4). Their leader, Gruk Halfear, has claimed the flask on the pedestal and keeps within reach of it. The orcs have not gone past the north door; the whispering beyond frightens them. If a raider fled here from the Mosaic Hall (room 2), the orcs are ready behind the barricade (half cover).

Encounter: 1 Orc War-Chief and 1 Orc Raider. If the hero has not taken the flask, Gruk drinks it as a Bonus Action the first time he is Bloodied, gains the Invisible condition, and fights on.

Treasure: the Potion of Invisibility (the flask on the pedestal), and 75 gp in the orcs' loot sack behind the barricade.

Exits: Inner Archive (10, door), Steward's Room (4, door). The door in the middle of the north wall opens into the Inner Archive. The broken door in the middle of the west wall leads back to the Steward's Room.

name: Inner Archive
read: A wide, low room, lined floor to ceiling with racks of scroll cases. Each case is capped in tarnished silver and stamped with a tiny crown. The dust here lies thick and unbroken. The whispering is louder now, coming from the north, and you can almost make out words: names, dates, the endings of things. A stone door with a carved crown stands in the west wall, and wooden doors stand to the north and south.
notes:
The heart of the archive: the fair copies of every prophecy Mother Ysolde ever spoke, centuries of them. The racks hold real lore; a hero who spends 10 minutes reading can ask the GM one question about the past of the dark wood and get a true answer. No one has entered since the scribes died, and the orcs have not dared the north door from room 9.

No encounter.

Treasure: a Potion of Greater Healing and 100 gp in a silver-capped reliquary niche at the end of the north rack.

Exits: Oracle's Gallery (11, door), Pedestal Hall (9, door), Hall of the Stone Door (8, locked stone door). The door in the middle of the north wall opens into the Oracle's Gallery. The door in the middle of the south wall opens into the Pedestal Hall. The stone door in the middle of the west wall opens into the Hall of the Stone Door; from this side it opens freely.

name: Oracle's Gallery
read: A long, narrow gallery runs north. Along both walls stand stone statues of women seated on thrones, each face hidden behind a veil of grey cloth stiff with age. The veils stir slightly, as if the statues were breathing. The air is warm and wet and smells of rot. Near the south end of the west wall a heavy stone bar lies across a plain stone door. To the east, an open passage leads toward the whispering.
notes:
The statues show the seers who came before Mother Ysolde. The Grey Rot has rooted in the stone behind their veils, and they exhale it when the living pass.

Trap: Rot Mist

  • Trigger: a creature reaches the middle of the gallery, between the statues.
  • Find: DC 16 Wisdom (Perception) notices grey dust puffing from under the veils in time with the stirring, and grey stains on the floor between them.
  • Effect: DC 16 Constitution saving throw [[/save con 16]]; [[/damage 6d10 necrotic]] on a failure, half on a success. The mist fills the gallery once and then the statues must breathe again; it triggers again 10 minutes later.
  • Disarm or avoid: Burn the veils with fire (an action per side, which spends that side's mist), or hold breath and move fast (still triggers but with Advantage on the save), or stay close to the walls behind the statues with a DC 16 Dexterity (Stealth) check.

The stone bar on the west door lifts from this side with no check; once lifted, the door to the Hall of the Stone Door (room 8) opens freely, giving a short way back.

No encounter.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Inner Archive (10, door), Throne of the Oracle (12, open passage), Hall of the Stone Door (8, sealed door). The door in the middle of the south wall leads back to the Inner Archive. The open passage in the middle of the east wall leads to the Throne of the Oracle. The barred stone door at the south end of the west wall opens into the Hall of the Stone Door once the bar is lifted.

name: Throne of the Oracle
read: A great round chamber rises around a stone dais. On it sits a figure in a robe stitched all over with open, staring eyes. What can be seen of her body is grey and crumbling, her face eaten half away, yet her lips move without pause, and the whispering pours from her. Four tall piles of scrolls ring the dais, each beside an iron brazier burning with low blue flame. Grey dust drifts in the air like falling snow.
notes:
The end of the adventure. The figure is Mother Ysolde, The Leper Oracle. She died on this seat, and the Grey Rot keeps her undead. The scroll piles are her original prophecies, the ones the scribes copied from. She speaks prophecies of the hero's own death in the second person throughout the fight. The braziers give dim light across the chamber.

Encounter: The Leper Oracle, alone. She is an Epic Boss and never leaves the dais willingly.

The prophecy piles. Four piles of scrolls ring the dais. The hero can burn a pile with an action and any fire (a torch, a fire spell, a flask of oil lit), or tip a pile into its brazier with an action and a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check. Each time a pile burns, the Oracle screams and loses her next Response. When two piles have burned, she loses her Epic Boss Resistance for the rest of the fight.

Treasure: the Robe of Eyes (the Oracle's robe, taken from her body after she falls; the Grey Rot leaves it when she dies) and The Oracle's Last Prophecy, a sealed scroll in her lap.

Exits: Oracle's Gallery (11, open passage). The open passage in the middle of the west wall leads back to the Oracle's Gallery.
